exposure: antenatal late preterm steroids (ALPS) administration (including partial course and timing relative to delivery)
mode of birth (cesarean delivery vs. vaginal)
cohort: Pregnant patients delivering late preterm (34(0/7) to 36(6/7) weeks gestational age) at a tertiary care medical center between October 2017 and September 2020 who received one or two doses of antenatal late preterm steroids, excluding those with prior BMZ treatment, pregestational diabetes, anomalous fetus, or multifetal gestation.
finding: Neonatal hypoglycemia was most frequent when delivery occurred between 12 and 35 hours after the first betamethasone dose, and was also associated with increasing birthing parent age, cesarean delivery, and delivery after labor onset.
mod_finding: Neonatal hypoglycemia and NICU admission rates were increased with cesarean delivery and with shorter ALPS exposure to delivery time.
